what: Beryl LAN now carries verified Jetson SSH and KVM keyboard control; C270 still capture works on Jetson.
why: Make local control repeatable without VPN and preserve capture instructions with explicit video, power and arm-acceptance limits.
details: Jetson SSH remains at 192.168.8.136 with system running. Moved KVM 192.168.8.166 accepts the saved credential; Escape woke the Jetson lock screen, visibly verified through the Jetson-hosted C270. Old 192.168.2.2 is unreachable. Mouse request acceptance alone did not verify delivery. C270 046d:0825 uses uvcvideo: video0 capture/video1 metadata. Non-root GStreamer 1.24.2 produced 640x480 JPEGs after 30-frame warm-up; first frame was dark during exposure startup. Mac camera indices are obsolete. Reusable Linux helper passed inventory and a bounded 30-frame snapshot on Jetson with a stable alias and a new output directory; its own JPEG was visually verified and all four test methods passed on the Jetson in 0.020 s. Four private output copies match target hashes. Timing metadata is Jetson-local receipt timing, not a live feed. Network no longer depends on Mac Ethernet sharing, but KVM power still comes from the Mac. Same-LAN access needs no Tailscale or subnet change; optional off-site routing is unconfigured. Video cable expected in the morning: required direction is Jetson DisplayPort to KVM HDMI, with compatibility/image still unverified. No HDMI video or arm hardware milestone claimed. A brief interruption resolved at the original addresses without LAN reset/renumber: strict SSH and KVM authentication passed again, with 58 minutes Jetson uptime and no reboot. Exact cause remains unknown; native Wi-Fi settings confirmed Beryl. The exact historical runtime recovery script, dependency closure and result are archived with hashes and explicit reuse limits.
